solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: B&B kept by former footballer — one by the sea?

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it, so the footballer's name wraps round the pair of letters

parts.note: Pele, the great Brazilian forward of the 1950s-70s
bed and breakfast abbreviated gives two Bs

explanation.surface: A retired football star runs a seaside bed-and-breakfast guesthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Pele is the Brazilian footballer. The definition is playful: 'one by the sea' points to a single stone on the beach, with the question mark flagging the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth stones lie in their thousands along a shingle beach, so each is one found by the sea.

clue.text: Favouring certain words in an old book

parts.note: pro means in favour of
verbs are one class of words

explanation.surface: Someone has a liking for particular words found in an antique volume.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a book of the Old Testament of the Bible, a collection of wise sayings.

clue.text: Women preferred by men allegedly led snob astray

indicators.note: going astray, the letters wander out of their order

explanation.surface: Fair-haired women who led a snobbish man off the straight path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges LED SNOB. The definition alludes to the film title 'Gentlemen Prefer Blondes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous film and novel title claims gentlemen prefer fair-haired women.

clue.text: American unit destroying half of what's written

indicators.note: half the word is wiped out, leaving its first half

parts.note: literature is written work

explanation.surface: An American measure that wrecks half of a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying half of' keeps the first five of the ten letters of LITERATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the US spelling of the metric unit of volume, so an American-spelt unit.

clue.text: One arriving outside place to deliver piece of electronic equipment

indicators.note: one piece stands outside the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: a comer is someone who comes or arrives
to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: A courier arrives at a house to drop off some electrical gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to deliver' is only a link here, though the surface makes it sound like the courier's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer is a standard example of an electronic device or machine.

clue.text: Ignore tree in ground in outdoor sport

indicators.note: ground means crushed and reduced, so the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to a tree in the field while playing an outdoor game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' (crushed) rearranges IGNORE TREE IN; 'in' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This cross-country sport has competitors navigating with map and compass, so it is an outdoor sport.

clue.text: Those of the same class — upper class?

definitions.meaning: people of the same age or status as each other
the nobility, the lords, as a group

explanation.surface: A social set, perhaps the posh ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'peer' as a member of the nobility, so a body of lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names one's equals in age or status; read differently, it is a set of nobles.

clue.text: How cooking should be done, as shown by kid holding a vessel

indicators.note: the kid holds the letter inside

parts.note: a tot is a small child
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A child carrying a pot shows how food ought to be cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as shown by' links definition to wordplay; the vessel is the urn, not a cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means cooked exactly right, which is how food ideally should be done.

clue.text: Old magistrates pause briefly when first woman enters

indicators.note: the woman goes into the shortened word
briefly says the word is cut short at the end

parts.note: a rest is a pause
Eve, the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Elderly officials take a short break as the first female member arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the last letter off the word for pause, leaving RES, before 'enters' adds the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Saxon and medieval England these were local officers who administered justice, so old magistrates.

clue.text: Portuguese location in which there's nothing left — nothing!

parts.note: zero, written as the letter O
port is the left side of a ship
zero again, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A Portuguese town so bare that nothing at all is left there.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'nothing' reads as emphasis but supplies the two Os either side of PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the older English name for Porto, the port city in northern Portugal.

clue.text: Gassy beer maybe for dog?

parts.note: aired, in the sense of having been given air or having gassed on about something
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Is a fizzy beer suitable to give a dog?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a beer-and-dog joke; the wordplay just reads the breed's name as AIRED ALE, a beer with air in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire, so it is one kind of canine.

clue.text: Talk or confer? That may be unusual for this decisive person

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the letters is called for, so they are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone who must decide everything wonders whether to talk or to consult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be unusual' rearranges TALK OR CONFER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obsessed with having their own way insists on making every decision, a domineering sort.

clue.text: I wondered about what to discard on hot summer nights

definitions.text: what to discard on hot summer nights

indicators.note: about signals moving the letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone muses over what bedding to throw off on sweltering nights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges I WONDERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick feather quilt is the bedcover you would kick off when the nights are warm.

clue.text: Look to preserve university fabric

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safely held, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

explanation.surface: An instruction to try to save some cloth belonging to a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to preserve' puts U inside GAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: This thin, open-weave material is used for dressings and curtains, so it is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Where digit in decimal number may go? It's immaterial

definitions.text: Where digit in decimal number may go?
definitions.meaning: literally, a digit can sit next to the decimal point
irrelevant, not relevant to the matter under discussion

explanation.surface: A maths question about placing a digit, followed by a dismissive aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: a digit written just alongside the dot in a decimal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means irrelevant, off the subject, which is what an immaterial point is.

clue.text: Censure one ultimately carpeted for misbehaving

indicators.note: the letters misbehave and stray out of line, so they are shuffled
ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone is told off and hauled up for bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E, the last letter of 'one'; 'for misbehaving' rearranges CARPETED to give the rest. 'Carpeted' (reprimanded) looks like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To express strong disapproval of something is to censure it.

clue.text: Pair restricting noise? One is blethering

definitions.note: one who is blethering, i.e. a person talking idly

indicators.note: the pair hems in the noise, holding it inside

parts.note: a rattle is a noise

explanation.surface: Two people trying to keep the noise down while one chatters on.
explanation.walkthrough: Blethering is Scottish for talking nonsense at length; the definition is the whole phrase 'One is blethering', a person who does so.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterer who talks foolishly and at length is one who blethers.

clue.text: Arachnid that could make parrots drop and die

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spider so dangerous it could kill birds outright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges PARROTS DROP and DIE together; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: These burrowing spiders build a hinged lid over their tunnel, so they belong to the arachnids.

clue.text: Came back with explanation as to why customer was cheated?

definitions.text: explanation as to why customer was cheated?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, the sales rep told a falsehood

explanation.surface: Someone responded with a reason why a shopper was swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as REP LIED: the salesman lied, which explains the cheated customer.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer or respond is to come back with something.

clue.text: Noise with water rising in Warwick?

definitions.note: the first name of a novelist, so the answer is a surname

indicators.note: the reversed water goes inside the noise

parts.note: a ding is a ringing noise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: pee is slang for urine, passing water

explanation.surface: A sound of floodwater rising in the town of Warwick.
explanation.walkthrough: Warwick looks like the English town, but it is the first name of Warwick Deeping, an English novelist (Sorrell and Son); 'rising' reverses the water in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname completes the name of the popular interwar writer Warwick Deeping.

clue.text: Bishop to get cross, an explosive type?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
anger is the state of getting cross

explanation.surface: A churchman losing his temper, a volatile character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive type' suggests a hothead; it is a firework. In Britain a banger is also a sausage or an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A firecracker that goes off with a loud report is one sort of explosive device.

clue.text: Fruit drink containing pip I disposed of

indicators.note: the drink holds the other letters within it

parts.note: ale is a drink

indicators.note: the letter I is got rid of from the word pip

explanation.surface: A fruity drink that had its pip removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed of' takes the I out of the word pip, leaving PP for the drink to contain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the common orchard fruit, one of the best-known examples of fruit.

clue.text: Enjoyment lady has with holy books — sitting on this?

parts.note: fun means enjoyment
a dame is a lady, also a title for a woman
NT is the New Testament, a collection of holy books

explanation.surface: A woman reading scripture for pleasure, sitting comfortably.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bottom one sits on; the question mark marks it as a playful hint rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a formal or jocular term for the buttocks, which is what a person sits on.

clue.text: Sailor needs a lot of sheets of pink paper for his behind!

definitions.note: nautical term for at or toward the stern

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

parts.words: lot of sheets of pink paper
parts.note: the Financial Times, a newspaper printed on pink paper

explanation.surface: A sailor uses plenty of pink newspaper for wiping his bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, Britain's business daily on pink newsprint, where this puzzle appeared. 'His behind' teases as a bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: This nautical term means toward the stern, so it means behind on a ship.

clue.text: Pulled a face, seeing club surrounded by grating

indicators.note: the club is enclosed by the grating, inside it

parts.note: a grid is a grating of bars
a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon

explanation.surface: Someone winced on seeing a club stuck behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing' is a link word; 'club' is the weapon, not a society.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a contorted expression of pain or disgust is the same as pulling a face.

clue.text: Moving away from centre, being leftist not Conservative

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation must be left out of the word

parts.note: a radical is someone on the far left

explanation.surface: A politician drifting from the centre ground, now left-wing rather than Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops C from RADICAL. The political surface makes 'centre' look like the political centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Radial movement goes outward along a radius, directly away from a central point.

clue.text: Poor Americans showing evidence of getting hot behind the collar?

definitions.meaning: a US term for poor white rural labourers

definitions.text: showing evidence of getting hot behind the collar?
definitions.meaning: literally, having skin flushed scarlet at the back of the neck, from sunburn or anger

explanation.surface: Impoverished Americans whose necks flush with heat or temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from the sunburnt necks of field workers; 'hot under the collar' (angry) is twisted to 'behind'.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is American slang for working-class white rural people, often poor.

clue.text: Old actor to move unsteadily, losing heart

indicators.note: the middle of the word is where a letter is dropped, its heart

parts.note: to stagger is to totter or move unsteadily

explanation.surface: An elderly thespian tottering about, having lost his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' drops one of the central Gs of STAGGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stager is a dated word for a stage player, as in the phrase 'old stager'.
